Slagelse Kirurgi is a surgical department in Denmark that has become the subject of quality-control scrutiny due to an exceptionally high re-operation rate. According to 2024 data from the Danish Inflammatory Bowel Disease Database (DANIBD), the department reports a re-operation rate of 50% for surgical procedures — a figure that significantly exceeds the national development target of 8%[^src1]. This measure, which tracks the proportion of patients requiring a second surgery within 30 days of their initial procedure, is a key indicator of surgical quality and safety in the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).

The re-operation rate reported by Slagelse Kirurgi stands as a marked outlier in the national quality-assurance landscape. The gap between the department's 50% rate and the 8% benchmark suggests either a difference in patient population, surgical technique, post-operative care protocols, or case-selection practices compared to other surgical centers participating in the DANIBD registry. This data point appears in the context of DANIBD's broader annual monitoring of both biological medicine uptake (F-calprotectin measurement compliance) and surgical outcomes across Denmark's IBD treatment network.
